draft.title: Equity of access to health care
card: Equity of access means people with the same need can get the same quality of care. It is about fairness, not about everyone getting identical treatment.
A public system does not remove every barrier. Costs, such as gap fees and travel, can put people off seeking care.
Long waiting times can delay care. Distance can also be a barrier, as people in remote areas may live hours from a hospital or specialist.
Language can be a barrier too. A person who cannot follow the advice given, or cannot book an appointment, may go without care they need.
draft.remember: Even with a public system, cost, time, distance and language can stop people getting the care they need.

a.q: Which situation shows a barrier to equity of access to health care?
opts: A farmer lives six hours from the nearest specialist
Two people with the same illness get the same medicine
A hospital treats the sickest patients before others
A clinic opens a new ward for children with asthma
a.why: Long distance to a specialist can stop a person getting care they need, so it is a barrier to access. Treating the sickest first is not a barrier. It matches care to need, which is what equity means.
a.clue: Which one makes it harder for someone to reach care?

b.q: Tran recently arrived in Australia and speaks little English. He has a Medicare card but often skips doctor visits. Which is the most likely barrier to his access?
opts: Language, as he may not follow or book appointments
Cost, as Medicare card holders must pay every fee
Waiting times, as new arrivals are always seen last
Distance, as Medicare only covers city doctors
b.why: Tran has a Medicare card, and the problem is understanding and booking care, so language is the barrier. Cost is tempting, but holding a card does not mean he pays every fee, and the case gives no sign that cost is the problem.
b.clue: What does the case say about Tran, apart from his card?

a.best: A farmer lives six hours from the nearest specialist

b.best: Language, as he may not follow or book appointments

problems.detail: The three wrong options use absolute words ('must pay every fee', 'only covers city doctors', 'always seen last'), while the right option is the only one with a hedge ('may'). A student could rule out the distractors or spot the answer from wording alone, without knowing the idea.
The words 'must', 'only' and 'always' appear in options, but the card speaks of barriers that 'can' put people off or delay care.

Cost, as he may be unable to pay the clinic's fees
Waiting times, as he may wait weeks to see a doctor
Distance, as he may need to travel hours to a doctor
